newsitem.title: CANADA: Stranded Arctic cruise passengers evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Stranded Arctic cruise passengers evacuated.

text.p: About 150 tourists were finally taken off a German cruise ship on Thursday after being stranded for a week in Canada's Arctic after the liner ran aground.

The Canadian Coast Guard said about 120 passengers aboard the luxury liner Hanseatic were being transferred to the Russian ice-breaker Kaptain Dranitsyn. They were expected to continue their Arctic cruise on Friday, but the remaining passengers decided to return home and were being flown south to catch flights.
The Hanseatic ran aground on a gravel bar near King William Island in Canada's Northwest Passage last Thursday. No one was hurt but attempts to refloat the vessel failed.

Most passengers are German, with about 40 Americans. Canada's Coast Guard said there were 153 passengers in all, while cruise operator Hanseatic Tours of Hamburg said there were 149. The ship also has a crew of about 115.

Passengers were being transferred from the Hanseatic in a complex operation involving boats, planes and buses. They were taken in small boats to a nearby air strip from where they were to fly to the town of Cambridge Bay on Victoria Island.
Buses would then take them to a dock where the Russian ship was waiting. Baggage and supplies were also transferred.
Coast Guard spokesman Andries Blouw said some snow had fallen and temperatures were just above freezing. "We're confident the operation will come across nicely," he said.

While they were stuck on the grounded Hanseatic, passengers passed the time with expeditions to the nearby island, where they held barbecues. Amenities on the Hanseatic include lounges and dining rooms, exercise facilities, sauna and massage, duty-free shopping, swimming pool and library.

The 404-foot (123-metre) ship was built in 1993 to the highest international standards for ice-going passenger vessels. Tug boats were on their way to free the ship, which will be taken to Montreal for repairs, the Coast Guard said.
Investigators will probe the cause of the grounding.
